checks.name: Extra container on igf-wa node: docker-socket-proxy (outside the stack compose)
checks.evidence: igf-wa runs tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest (v0.4.2), restart unless-stopped, /var/run/docker.sock:ro, default bridge network, NO compose project labels (started outside compose). Absent from both compose files and from the sanctioned-deviations list. Likely deliberate host infra (matches the toolbox-box socket-proxy pattern) but on the default bridge it is reachable from other bridge containers and grants read access to the Docker API; wa-mancer runtime could not be checked for an equivalent. Needs a ruling: either sanction it (and document why it runs un-composed on the default bridge) or move it into a declared stack on an isolated network.

result.summary: Stack compose parity is effectively 1:1. After applying the sanctioned renames (wa-mancer→igf-wa names/paths/images, wamancer→igfwa cache prefix), a comment-stripped structural diff of ssh wa-mancer:/opt/wa-mancer/stack/docker-compose.yml vs ssh igf-wa:/opt/igf-wa/stack/docker-compose.yml leaves only: (1) caddy service + edge network + cloudflare_api_token secret dropped, (2) SERVER_URL https://api.welcomdeal.ma → http://100.112.39.73:8080, (3) evolution-api gains a loopback-only 127.0.0.1:8080 port publish for tailscale serve, (4) worker EVOLUTION_API_URL uses the compose service name instead of the container name (functionally equivalent DNS), (5) worker/redis block ordering swapped (no semantics). All are covered by sanctioned deviations 3 and 4. Postgres and redis blocks are byte-identical post-rename, including the load-bearing one-line redis command that prevents the silent-passwordless-redis regression, all 9 DATABASE_SAVE_* flags, DEL_INSTANCE=false/DEL_TEMP_INSTANCES=true, the 2.3.7 source-built pin, per-service healthchecks, cap_drop ALL hardening, and journald logging with {{.Name}} tags. Runtime on igf-wa matches the compose (all four containers healthy, evolution loopback-only). ONE FLAG: an un-composed tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy v0.4.2 container runs on the igf-wa host (docker.sock:ro, default bridge, no compose labels) — not in either compose file and not on the sanctioned list; needs explicit sanctioning or relocation into a declared, network-isolated stack. Cosmetic note: the igf-wa compose header comment still says the worker service will be 'added when the worker port lands' although the worker service is present and healthy — stale comment worth fixing.

result.summary: Evolution runtime is at full behavior-critical parity with WA Mancer: all 21 flags in the audited set (DATABASE_SAVE_* x9, DEL_INSTANCE/DEL_TEMP_INSTANCES, CACHE_* x4, CONFIG_SESSION_PHONE_* x2, QRCODE_* x2, WEBHOOK_GLOBAL_ENABLED, LOG_* x3, TELEMETRY, AUTHENTICATION_EXPOSE_IN_FETCH_INSTANCES, LANGUAGE) are value-identical, and both images are built from evolution-foundation/evolution-api tag 2.3.7 (ours verified running via docker inspect; wa-mancer via compose since its docker socket is root-only). Sanctioned deviations only for SERVER_URL topology, CACHE_REDIS_PREFIX_KEY naming, image name, and an added DATABASE_CONNECTION_CLIENT_NAME. One unsanctioned but currently inert gap: CACHE_REDIS_URI exists in WA Mancer's evolution.env (evolution_redis_uri.sops) but is entirely absent from our container env — harmless while CACHE_REDIS_ENABLED=false, latent breakage if the redis cache is ever enabled; add it to /opt/igf-wa/secrets/evolution.env. result.summary: Worker source is a clean 1:1 port. Truth baseline verified (local repo == live wa-mancer VPS byte-for-byte). Of 22 ported files, 10 are byte-identical to truth; the 12 differing files contain ONLY sanctioned hunks: public.->whatsapp. schema qualification everywhere (SQL, RPCs, realtime channel, supabase-js .schema('whatsapp')), naming (application_name igf-wa-worker, bucket default whatsapp-media), and the three sanctioned worker deltas (platformLogPull dropped with zero dangling references, WORKER_REAP_ORPHANS observe-only gate correctly wired before deleteEvolutionInstance with runtime env=false, unhandledRejection log-only handler added). Zero unsanctioned deviations, zero leftover public.* references, and the deployed tree on igf-wa is md5-identical to the ported tree across all 22 files. Residual 'wa-mancer' literals (WORKER_ID default, x-wa-mancer-secret header, two comments) are byte-identical to truth and inert or protocol-consistent at runtime (WORKER_ID overridden to igf-wa1-worker-1 via compose).

All three spot-checks hold: is_group is GENERATED STORED with the identical (remote_jid ~~ '%@g.us') expression on both sides, key_id exists on messages+conversations (sanctioned crypto seam), number_pacing_state defaults match exactly. result.summary: Queue-dispatch semantics are at full parity. All 8 dispatch-critical functions (queue_claim_next, queue_mark_sent, queue_mark_failed, queue_mark_dead, pacing_take_token, dispatch_gate_check, worker_heartbeat, worker_claim_instance_leases) are byte-identical between WA Mancer public.* and our whatsapp.* after normalizing schema qualifiers — a clean diff over the full 364-line pg_get_functiondef dump. NOTIFY plumbing matches: _outbound_queue_notify body and both outbound_queue notify triggers (INSERT when status='queued'; UPDATE when old<>'queued' AND new='queued') are identical; media_fetch_ready is emitted from enqueue_media_fetch on both sides (no trigger on media_fetch_jobs anywhere). Only two deviations found, both sanctioned: bucket literal wamancer-media -> whatsapp-media in enqueue_media_fetch (naming #3) and is_admin() -> is_wa_admin(instance) in the two admin-path emitters force_dispatch_now/admin_requeue_dead (identity #2, with a trivial error-message reorder for nonexistent queue ids in admin_requeue_dead).
